title: Attempt on Ross modulation monotonicity and a criterion for Cox workload ordering
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Explicit model calculation, comparison identities and remaining hypothesis obstruction Result: A complete candidate refutation of universal monotonicity is in the proof packet. Use deterministic unit service, epsilon=1/10000, and a1024-state clockwise CTMC with first Fourier eigenvalue -tan(pi/1024)+i. The intensity is epsilon*[2+cos(2pi*X/1024+pi/2048)], with distinct positive state values. A workload-minus-parallel-shot monotonicity argument gives the uniform expansion w(c)=epsilon+2epsilon^2+(epsilon^2/2)*integral_0^1(1-u)*exp[-c*u*tan(pi/1024)]*cos(c*u)du+R_c, where0<=R_c<=27epsilon^3/[2(1-3epsilon)]. It follows exactly that w(3pi)-w(2pi)>epsilon^2*2491/1612800>0. Check: The second-order kernel1-u is independently recovered by integrating the interaction workload of two arrivals over the age of the younger one. The proof bounds the remainder through domination by a stable homogeneous M/D/1 queue, rather than numerically fitting a light-traffic series. The rational lower-bound arithmetic is recorded separately. Obstruction: Universal monotonicity has a full counterexample candidate, but the necessary-and-sufficient condition requested in the same source problem remains open here. Earlier Ross-type literature, including Miyoshi-Rolski2004 and Heyman, must be compared in full before novelty is claimed. No independent review is claimed.

title: Attempt on Torus spanning-tree dual homotopy distribution
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Torus spanning-tree dual homotopy distribution structural reduction or obstruction Result: On a toroidal N-vertex square grid, E=2N and there are N faces. Removing the N-1 primal tree edges leaves N+1 dual edges. The dual complement is connected, so its first Betti number is(N+1)-N+1=2. This explains two independent topological cycles but does not itself specify the triple of simple-loop homotopy classes. Check: Euler's formula on the torus gives V-E+F=0. Dual connectivity follows because a separating primal-dual cut would correspond to a cycle contained in the primal tree, which is impossible. The cycle-rank formula is E-V+1 for a connected finite graph. Obstruction: Rank2 determines neither winding slopes nor their probabilities. A scalar Laplacian determinant counts all spanning trees without resolving this joint topological information.

title: Attempt on Fluctuations and large deviations of intermediate level sets of the 2D DGFF
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Second-order expansion of E[|level set|] by the local CLT for the DGFF at a point, then a variance computation from the two-point Gaussian density. Result: The first-order correction to the mean is computable: with h_x ~ N(0, g log N + O(1)) the mean of the level-set size is N^{2(1-lambda^2)} times (c + O((log N)^{-1/2})) where the (log N)^{-1/2} term comes from the Gaussian tail with the boundary correction G_N(x,x) - g log N. The variance is dominated by pairs at distance N^{1-lambda^2 t} for t in (0,1) and its exponent is 2(1-lambda^2) + something strictly positive, so the normalised fluctuation is not of CLT type but is driven by the field at mesoscopic scales; the natural conjecture is that the fluctuation is Z^D_lambda-mixed Gaussian with variance proportional to the integral of e^{2 alpha lambda h} over a scale window, but I could not close the identification of the mixing measure. Obstruction: No local limit theorem for pairs at every mesoscopic distance uniformly; the fluctuation law is a functional of the whole scale ladder, not of one scale.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0002-fluctuations-and-large-deviations-of-intermediate-level-sets-of-the-2d
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

title: Attempt on Fluctuations and large deviations of intermediate level sets of the 2D DGFF (corrected)
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD (SUPERSEDING REVISION 2026-09-07 12:4x after the Codex holder's review), author-checked only. CORRECTION of C0002-A001. With Var h_x = g log N + O(1) and threshold 2 sqrt(g) lambda log N, P(h_x >= threshold) = exp(-2 lambda^2 log N)/(sqrt(2 pi) 2 lambda sqrt(log N)) (1 + o(1)), so the mean size of the intermediate level set is of order N^{2 - 2 lambda^2}/sqrt(log N), not a constant times N^{2(1 - lambda^2)} as A001 wrote; the (log N)^{-1/2} is the leading normalisation, not a correction term. The rest of A001 (variance dominated by mesoscopic pairs, mixing-measure identification open) stands with this normalisation. Key identity: E|level set| = c N^{2-2 lambda^2} (log N)^{-1/2} (1+o(1)) with c = 1/(2 sqrt(2 pi) lambda) times the boundary-correction factor. Standing obstruction: see the earlier attempt; the correction above replaces the flawed step only.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0002-fluctuations-and-large-deviations-of-intermediate-level-sets-of-the-2d

title: Attempt on Transience of the dual infinite Boltzmann map for a in [2, 5/2)
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Compare with the a in (3/2, 2) proof via first-passage percolation and with the recurrence criterion via degree growth. Result: For a < 2 the source proves transience through a finite-energy flow built from the fpp-distance structure, using that face degrees along the peeling are heavy-tailed enough (the dual has vertices of huge degree, giving 'highways'). For a >= 2 the degree of the dual's root is lighter tailed and the map is 'dilute'; the known results are: the primal map is recurrent for all a (bounded degrees, Gurel-Gurevich-Nachmias), and the dual is transient for a < 2. For a in [2,5/2) the dual has volume growth exponent (a - 1/2)/(a - 3/2)... the volume of balls in the dual grows polynomially with degree 2 x (a-1/2)/(a-3/2)?? at a = 5/2 the dual is the UIPQ-type map with quartic volume growth, known recurrent (Gurel-Gurevich-Nachmias again since the dual of a map with bounded degrees is... no: the dual of the UIPQ has unbounded degrees but is recurrent by Lee's or by Gurel-Gurevich-Nachmias's extension to exponential-tail degrees). So at the endpoint a = 5/2 the answer is recurrence, provided the dual's root degree has an exponential tail, which holds for the UIPQ. At a = 2 the degrees have a tail of index 1 (heavy), suggesting transience persists. Hence the conjectural picture is a transition inside [2, 5/2), and the open question as stated (transient for all a in [2,5/2)) is likely FALSE near 5/2 and true near 2; the right question is the location of the transience threshold a_t in [2, 5/2]. Recorded as a partial obstruction with a proposed refinement. Key identity: At a = 5/2 the dual is recurrent (exponential-tail degrees); at a slightly above 2 degrees have tail index near 1, favouring transience; a threshold a_t in (2, 5/2] is expected. Obstruction: The tail index of the dual root degree crosses the Gurel-Gurevich-Nachmias regime inside the interval; the threshold is not located.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0059-transience-of-the-dual-infinite-boltzmann-map-for-a-in-2-5-2

title: Open problem: Asymptotic expansion of the critical value of the Hamming graph

title: Attempt on Asymptotic expansion of the critical value of the Hamming graph
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Compute a_2(d) by the cycle-correction method as a check, and identify why the expansion truncates at d/3. Result: On K_n^d every vertex has degree d(n-1); at p = lambda/(d(n-1)) the exploration is close to a branching process; the first correction to the branching ratio comes from triangles: each vertex lies in d (n-1)(n-2)/2 triangles (all in one coordinate line), so the effective number of NEW vertices reached in two steps is reduced by a relative amount of order 1/d... normalising, the triangle correction is of relative order (n-2)/(d(n-1)) ~ 1/d, not 1/n, so it shifts p_c at relative order 1/d which is absorbed into a_1(d)?? The source states a_1(d) = 1/d exactly and the corrections are in powers of 1/n, so the d-dependence at fixed order is packaged into a_i(d). The triangle correction: the branching process approximation counts each vertex's d(n-1) neighbours; the neighbours along the same coordinate line are mutually adjacent (a clique K_n), so a cluster exploring along a line finds n-1 vertices at once; this is a finite-size correction of relative order 1/n at each step, giving a_2(d) of order 1 in d; the source's Federico et al. result identifies it. The truncation at d/3 comes from the window width: the critical window of the Hamming graph has width V^{-1/3} = n^{-d/3} in p (relative), so terms beyond order n^{-d/3} are inside the window and meaningless as an expansion of a single critical value; this explains the O(n^{-1-d/3}) error and the number of meaningful terms d/3. Beyond this structural explanation and the second-order term, I did not compute a_3(d); it would need the 4-cycle and two-triangle corrections on the Hamming graph, where 4-cycles through a vertex number about d(d-1)(n-1)^2/2 (two coordinates) plus in-line ones. Key identity: Only terms above the critical window width n^{-d/3} are meaningful, which explains the truncation index d/3. Obstruction: Third-order cycle corrections on K_n^d not computed.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0083-asymptotic-expansion-of-the-critical-value-of-the-hamming-graph
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

title: Attempt on One-sided zero-one laws for one-dimensional excited random walks
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Check whether the ergodic-environment argument for the two-sided statement (Theorem 2.3/3.2) localises to one side. Result: The two-sided 0-1 law (range infinite or not) follows from stationarity of the environment plus a Borel-Cantelli over the sites visited; the one-sided event {sup X_n = infinity} is not invariant under the natural shifts because the walk started at 0 and the environment to the left matter. Under (SE) and (EL) the source notes (3.4) and (3.5) are equivalent, so the question is the 0-1 property itself. A sufficient condition beyond Theorem 3.10: if the environment is i.i.d. and the walk is 'monotone' in the environment (Proposition 4.2 style coupling, which needs (POS1) or its mirror), then P_0(sup X_n = infinity) is a monotone function of a product measure, and the event {sup X_n = infinity} is a tail event with respect to the environment on the right half-line only if the walk's right excursions are determined by the right environment, which fails because the walk can be pushed back by the left environment. I tried the following route: under (SE) and (WEL), the event {sup X_n = infinity} is invariant under the environment shift restricted to trajectories that reach every site to the right, so conditionally on reaching site k the probability of eventually reaching k+1 is the same functional of the shifted environment; if the walk reaches every site to the right a.s. on the event, an ergodicity argument along the sequence of first-hitting times gives 0-1. The gap is exactly that 'reaching k' depends on the environment left of k through the returns. No general 0-1 law obtained; the reduction to a renewal-type ergodicity along right-hitting times is recorded. Obstruction: Left environment influences right excursions; no shift invariance of the one-sided event.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0128-one-sided-zero-one-laws-for-one-dimensional-excited-random-walks
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

title: Attempt on Random complex phase-retrieval injectivity at 4M-5 measurements
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Complete M=2 obstruction via Hermitian lifting Result: For M=2 the matrix has three complex Gaussian rows. Almost surely these span C^2. The real-linear measurement map from the four-dimensional Hermitian 2-by-2 space to R^3 has a nonzero kernel element H. H cannot be positive or negative semidefinite: a_i^* H a_i=0 for a spanning set would force H=0. Thus H has one positive and one negative eigenvalue and can be written xx^*-yy^* with noncollinear x,y. Their three intensity measurements agree. Hence p_2=0. Check: Dimension gives a nonzero H without assuming generic rank three; the spanning condition rules out semidefinite kernel elements. Spectral decomposition independently verifies equal squared magnitudes. Obstruction: For M>2 a nonzero kernel matrix need not have rank at most two with one eigenvalue of each sign. The requisite low-rank intersection probability remains unresolved.

title: Attempt on Invariant monotone coupling of free and wired uniform spanning forests
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Invariant monotone coupling under an amenable action Result: Start with a monotone coupling of the two invariant forest laws under a countable amenable action. Average its translates over a Folner sequence. The product space of two edge configurations is compact, the prescribed marginals are unchanged, and the order relation is closed. A subsequential weak limit is therefore still a monotone coupling and is invariant because translation changes each average by at most its Folner boundary ratio. Check: The argument averages probability measures, not individual configurations, so convexity preserves the marginals and the monotone support. Compactness is available for a countable locally finite edge set. Obstruction: For a nonamenable acting group there is no Folner averaging sequence. Existence of an arbitrary monotone coupling does not by itself produce an invariant one.
